newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to decide soon on N.Korea food aid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to decide soon on N.Korea food aid.

text.p: The United States said on Wednesday it would make a decision very soon on a $95 million U.N. World Food Programme request for aid to North Korea.

"I would expect, given the severity of the food situation and the urgency of the appeal, that the United States government decision would be made very soon but I can't predict when that day will be," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
Burns said there was a serious and worsening food shortage in North Korea and the evidence was too great to argue otherwise.

"We understand the severity of the problem and we understand the World Food Program appeal is going to be focussed on children age six and under, and surely we all have a humanitarian imperitive in any kind of situation like this to try and be as helpful as we can to young kids like that," he said.
The United States continued to talk with North Korea about a place and date for a second round of talks on foreign missile sales, Burns said.

The United States has made clear its concern over Pyongyang's missile sales to Iran and Syria and said progress on this issue was critical to improved U.S.-North Korean ties. The first round of missile talks took place in April 1996.
